messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Multiple definitions for the same node
parts:
Abby, from a quick glance, it does seem you shouldn't be getting this error here, since your definition of log_nmortality is not inside the loop over (k = 1:nsize).

One possible issue, do you have another variable elsewhere in your model called "nmortality"?  If so, and furthermore it's declared using a log() link function (on the right-hand-side of the declaration), then your declaration of log_nmortality might be clashing with the "lifted node" that nimble creates under the hood.  Without seeing anything more of your code, that's my best guess as to what's going on.

If this doesn't help you, are you able to share a reproducible example of this?

Thanks,
Daniel


On Sun, Sep 24, 2023 at 11:05 PM Abigail Keller <agke...@berkeley.edu> wrote:
Hi,

I'm wondering if I can have some guidance with interpreting the following warning message when I build a model (i.e. nimbleModel()):

Warning message:
In genExpandedNodeAndParentNames3(debug = debug) :
  Multiple definitions for the same node. Did you forget indexing with 'k' on the left-hand side of 'log_nmortality[t - 1, i] ~ dnorm(mean = log_nmortality_mean, sd = log_nmortality_sd, lower_ = -Inf, upper_ = Inf, .tau = log_nmortality_sd^-2, .var = log_nmortality_sd * log_nmortality_sd)'?


This corresponds to the following part of my model, with the most relevant part in bold:

for(t in 2:ntime){
    for(i in 1:nsite){
     
      #p(captured at all)
      p[t-1,i,1:nsize] <- 1-exp(-(size_sel_norm(pmax=trapm_pmax,xmax=trapm_xmax,sigma=trapm_sigma,y=y[1:nsize])*no_m[t,i]+
                                    size_sel_log(pmax=trapf_pmax,k=trapf_k,midpoint=trapf_midpoint,y=y[1:nsize])*no_f[t,i]))
     
      for(k in 1:nsize){
       
        # multinomial distribution -- trap level, observed sample size
        counts[t,1:nobs,i,k] ~ dmulti(pic_trap[t,1:nobs,i,k], n_cap[t,i,k])
       
        #binomial distribution -- observed sample size
        n_cap[t,i,k] ~ dbinom(size = round(N[t,i,k]), prob = p[t-1,i,k])
       
      }
     
      # multiply next_N by lognmortality (with process error)
      N[t,i,1:nsize] <- next_N[t-1,i,1:nsize]*exp(-exp(log_nmortality[t-1,i]))
     
      # normally distributed logmortality process error
      log_nmortality[t-1,i] ~ dnorm(log_nmortality_mean, sd=log_nmortality_sd)
     
      # project to next time period
      next_N[t-1,i,1:nsize] <- kernel[1:nsize,1:nsize]%*%(N[t-1,i,1:nsize] - n_cap[t-1,i,1:nsize])
    }    
  }



Thanks!!!
Abby

Hi Daniel,

So sorry! I just caught my mistake -- I had set.seed() with an old version of the model where log_nmortality was inside the (k = 1:nsize) loop. That warning makes sense to me now.

Thanks so much for your response,
Abby
